collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DEPARTURES AND EXILE (DEP-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Leaving and being left: moving huts, short journeys, visitors going home, goodbyes done well and badly, homesickness, and the rare person who sails away for good. Choosing to leave is never a rejection of one's people, and choosing to stay is never a failure.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: The old hut where a villager grew up is being taken down: take one piece of it, or watch from a distance.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The old hut where (subject) grew up is finally being taken down. It's leaning, the roof is rotten, and it's dangerous; nobody disputes any of that. The builders are starting this morning. (subject) has come to watch, and is finding it harder than (subject.he/she) expected.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) asks the builders for one thing: the doorpost, worn smooth at just the height where small hands used to grab it and swing round into the hut. They save it carefully. (subject) stands it in a corner of (subject.his/her) own hut. It doesn't fit with anything else in there. It doesn't need to.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) sits a little way off and watches until the last beam comes down. (subject.He/she) doesn't cry. (subject.He/she) isn't sure what (subject.he/she) feels. When it's done, there's just a square of bare earth. A few weeks later, grass has grown over it, and (child), a child, is playing there, and (subject) finds that (subject.he/she) doesn't mind that at all.
